svg.desc: Banner for a paper on the Shannon entropy of random geometric graphs. Left: the unit square with connection radius r = 1. The shaded amber region, bounded by four circular arcs of radius 1 centred at the corners, is the universal region U_1: points within distance 1 of every point of the square, which are joined to every other vertex and so carry no positional information. Its area is 1 + pi/3 - sqrt(3), about 0.315. A dashed blue disc of radius 1 - 1/sqrt(2) at the centre is the smaller region used in the earlier conjectured coefficient (area about 0.270). The marked point (0.85, 0.5) is universal but lies outside that disc; a dotted line shows its distance to the farthest corner is below 1. Right: the coefficient of n log2 n against the radius r from 0 to sqrt(2), computed from the paper’s closed forms. The solid amber curve is the proved coefficient 2(1 - u_2(r)); the dashed blue curve is the earlier upper coefficient 2(1 - beta(r)). Both equal 2 for r up to sqrt(2)/2; above that the shaded gap shows the earlier value is too large. At r = 1 the values are 1.461 (earlier) and 2 sqrt(3) - 2 pi/3, about 1.370 (proved). The gap peaks at about 0.161, 18.7 percent of the earlier coefficient, near r = 1.13. The conjecture is refuted between sqrt(2)/2 and sqrt(2) and confirmed below.
svg.text: Universal points carry no information, so they cost no bits
Storing a random geometric graph takes d(1 − μ(Ur)) n log2 n bits: the true coefficient is smaller than the conjectured one
joined to everyone, costs no bits
uniform points · fixed radius · curves from the paper’s closed forms (Figure 1) · the conjecture is refuted for √2/2 < r < √2 and confirmed below
